In this tutorial you compute the capacitance between a square metal pad and
the ground plane around it. It has three pages:

1. **Prepare** (this page): set up a Palace Electrostatic calculation and
   write a run directory.
2. [**Run**](run.qmd): run Palace on that directory.
3. [**Analyze**](analyze.qmd): read the pad-to-ground capacitance.

The earlier reference run gave a value close to **95 fF**.

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
Build [the SimplePad model](../simplepad-model.qmd) and keep that Python
session open. You need `snapshot`, `surface_films` and `output_root` from it.
:::

## Step 1: Set up the electrostatic problem

Create an `ElectrostaticSim`. Make the pad a terminal and the ground plane
Ground:

```python
from scgsim.palace import ElectrostaticSim

run_id = "pad-capacitance-01"
sim = ElectrostaticSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(output_root / run_id)

sim.add_terminal("pad", net_id="pad")
sim.add_ground(net_id="ground")
sim.set_electrostatic(
    save_fields=1,
    unassigned_conductor_policy="error",
    exterior_boundary_policy="none",
)
sim.set_surface_epr(representation="B", specs=surface_films)
```

- `unassigned_conductor_policy="error"` stops the run if some metal belongs
  to neither the terminal nor Ground. That catches a forgotten Net early.
- `exterior_boundary_policy="none"` leaves the outer vacuum boundary
  ungrounded, so only the drawn ground plane is Ground.
- `set_surface_epr` is required before meshing, even for capacitance. The
  films do not change the capacitance.

## Step 2: Set the mesh and accuracy

```python
sim.set_mesh(refined_mesh_size=10.0, max_mesh_size=200.0)
sim.set_numerical(
    order=2, tolerance=1e-6, max_iterations=2000,
    amr_max_passes=10, amr_tolerance=0.02, amr_update_fraction=0.15,
    save_adapt_iterations=True, output_paraview=True,
)
mesh_path = sim.mesh()
config_path = sim.write_config()
```

Mesh sizes are in micrometres. `order=2` selects second-order finite elements.
With `amr_max_passes=10`, Palace refines the mesh up to ten times, stopping
early once its error estimate falls below `amr_tolerance`.

## Step 3: Write the run directory

SCGSim does not start Palace. It writes a self-contained run directory with the
mesh, the configuration and a launch script, so the solver can run on another
computer:

```python
handoff = sim.prepare_handoff(
    profile="direct-local",
    executable="palace",
    resources={"processes": 8, "threads": 1, "command_style": "wrapper"},
)
print(handoff.run_dir)
print(handoff.handoff_id)
```

Write down both printed values. The Analyze page uses `handoff_id` to confirm
that the results it loads came from this run directory.

Change `executable` and `resources` to match your Palace host. If your host
loads Palace through environment modules, add
`setup_commands=("module load palace",)`. See
[Run a prepared model](../../course/execute.qmd#palace) for all options.

## Use the notebook instead

The OrPen SC PDK provides this tutorial as one notebook,
[`palace_electrostatic.ipynb`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/blob/51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/palace_electrostatic.ipynb).
It calls the same SCGSim functions. Set `WORKFLOW_ACTION` to
`"prepare_handoff"` for this page, run Palace yourself, then switch to
`"analyze_handoff"` for the Analyze page.
